short: The subfield of AI focused on enabling computers to analyze, understand, translate, and generate human language.
eli5: Teaching computers how human words, grammar, and meaning work so they can read and talk with us.
example: Powering voice assistants, search engines, spellcheckers, and document summarizers.

short: Cleaning and normalizing raw text—handling whitespace, Unicode, punctuation, or casing—before feeding it to a model.
eli5: Washing and chopping vegetables before you start cooking so everything fits the recipe cleanly.
example: Stripping HTML tags and normalizing accented characters before indexing articles.

short: Splitting raw text into discrete units—words, subwords, or characters—that an NLP model can process numerically.
eli5: Breaking a long LEGO castle down into individual standard bricks before counting or rebuilding it.

short: A classic text representation that counts how often each word appears in a document while ignoring word order.
eli5: Cutting every word out of a page, tossing them into a paper bag, and counting how many of each word you have.
example: Representing movie reviews as word-count vectors to classify positive vs. negative sentiment.

short: Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency: a weighting score that highlights words frequent in one document yet rare across the corpus.
eli5: Giving higher importance to distinctive words like 'supernova' while downplaying common filler words like 'the'.
example: Keyword search engines ranking pages that uniquely mention a user's rare technical term.

short: Dense vector representations (such as Word2Vec or GloVe) trained so words appearing in similar contexts occupy nearby points in space.
eli5: Placing every word on a giant meaning map where 'coffee' sits right next to 'tea' and far from 'submarine'.
example: Famous vector arithmetic where vector('king') - vector('man') + vector('woman') lands near 'queen'.

short: An NLP task that detects and classifies real-world entities in text such as people, organizations, dates, and locations.
eli5: Highlighting a news article with colored markers: yellow for people, blue for places, and green for companies.
example: Extracting 'Ada Lovelace' [PERSON] and 'London' [LOCATION] from a biography paragraph.

short: Determining the emotional tone or attitude—such as positive, negative, or neutral—expressed in a piece of text.
eli5: Reading a customer review and telling right away whether the writer is thrilled, annoyed, or neutral.
example: Monitoring thousands of product reviews to spot sudden frustration after a software update.

short: Analyzing a sentence's grammatical structure to map parts of speech and how words syntactically depend on one another.
eli5: Diagramming a sentence in school to see which word is the noun, which is the verb, and who did what to whom.
example: Building a dependency tree showing that 'chased' connects subject 'cat' to object 'mouse'.

short: Automatically translating text or speech from one human language into another while preserving meaning and fluency.
eli5: An automated bilingual interpreter turning a Japanese menu into natural English on your phone.
example: Sequence-to-sequence Transformers translating legal contracts between Spanish and German.

short: Reducing inflected words to a shared base form—either by chopping suffixes (stemming) or looking up dictionary roots (lemmatization).
eli5: Grouping 'running', 'runs', and 'ran' under the single base idea 'run' so searches don't miss matches.

short: A contiguous sequence of n items (words or characters) extracted from text to capture local word order and phrases.
eli5: Reading a sentence through a sliding window two or three words wide so 'ice cream' stays together.
example: Bigram ('not', 'good') reversing the positive signal of 'good' in sentiment classification.
